source.sourceBoundary: Current manuscript and standing guidance only; earlier reviews and old Cosmic art were not read.

scenes.scene: Upper quarter: a vast crooked fork of opaque plum interstellar dust, close enough to see denser cloud folds, several weak inflowing ribbons. All gas, absolutely no bright stars or central disk. Keep the main fork cropped at top/left so it reads as extensive environment rather than a second isolated inventory cloud.

Upper quarter: open fan of numerous distant, separately luminous modest stars nested within broad remaining dark gas, not a compact triangular cluster. No jet, pillars, cleared cavity or bright glowing fringe yet. This is a broad nursery environment; do not copy any complete circular icon or include a separate close-up disk.

Upper quarter: a recognizable old spiral at far upperleft, its outer arm pulled into one broad hooked tidal tail arcing toward upperright, tenuous plum dark gas interleaved with widely spread modest stars. A diffuse nursery glow stays far inside the old arm, no resolved new tail cluster, no shell, no cold-knot target painted separately. Keep the hook recognizable across repeated views.

Upper quarter: a close oblique section through broad dusty orbital bands around an off-frame young star; dark near-side dusty notch and muted amber reflected edge. The star itself is OUTSIDE frame because it is an independently overlaid receiver. Fine dust only, no pebbles, planets, boulders, moons or rings. No spiral galaxy; this is a much smaller smooth disk region.

Upper quarter: same oblique stellar-disk inclination but broad cold outer annulus in subdued bluegray, thin diffuse icy-grain haze with a distant warm stellar glow outside upperleft frame. No giant planet anywhere, no moons, no rings, no circumplanetary disk. Only extensive environmental gas and dust so the separate fixed giant can be made and later retire without a duplicate.

Upper quarter: exceptionally quiet bluegreen interstellar field with a narrow fading dust streak entering from upperleft and a few very distant small stellar points. No resolved central star, no whole stellar disk, no planets, moons or rings. This background supports two different epochs of the same system, shown through separate icons and fixed line drawing; it must not paint a simultaneous planetary tableau.

Upper quarter: an immense mostly cleared outer stellar-system volume. A single tiny cream host light sits very far at upperleft, its inner planetary region unresolved and much smaller than the open space. A few delicate widely separated orbital dust wisps only at upperedge. No passing second star (it will be a separate receiver), no resolved planet/moon/rings, no comet, tail or escaped world. Make outer-system distances feel vast.

Upper quarter: inside a modest star cluster; scattered discrete amber/cream lights at varied separations in faint bluegreen haze, some distant pairs. None touch or explode. No giant central star, no bright collision, no expanding shell, no triangular outline. Target cluster/pairs are separate game art, so scenery is a cropped surrounding stellar field, not a duplicated compact cluster medallion.

Upper quarter: the same broad hooked tidal-tail environment viewed closer at its edge, sparse old cream and amber stars and quiet dense plum gas folds to one side. No explosion, no expanding shell or glowing shock, no reduced compact cluster already completed. Most massive bright blue stars must not dominate this view. Main interactive cluster is a separate open line asset.

Upper quarter: two elongated distorted stellar concentrations approach one another again, with worn incomplete spiral arcs and widespread cream/amber stars, irregular dark gas lanes newly arranged between them. Not a finished round elliptical galaxy. No intact old gas shell, no new starburst or central outflow; old original bright blue stars no longer dominate. Preserve a modest orange landmark near the outer left arc without making a giant star.

Upper quarter: broad thin bluegreen galactic halo with an oblique distant diffuse stellar glow at upperleft and three irregular very faint transparent gas folds across the upper edge. Sense of large sparse space surrounding a disturbed galaxy, not uniformly cold clouds. No jet, no plasma bubble, no hot cavity, no lifted cloudlets or fallback already visible. Leave specific matter and physical receivers to separate game art.
